summary: 4-month-old boy (born at 34 weeks) with an intermittent right groin/scrotal swelling on crying that reduces spontaneously. Infant inguinal hernias need prompt repair (herniotomy, no mesh) because the incarceration risk is highest in the first year; watchful waiting is not appropriate.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Swelling in the right groin when crying
inputs.hpi: Mother has noticed a swelling in the right groin extending towards the scrotum for 3 weeks, only when he cries or strains, and it goes away when he settles. Feeding well, no vomiting. Born at 34 weeks, no neonatal surgery.

exam.abdomen: Soft. Right inguinoscrotal swelling seen when crying, reduces spontaneously; thickened cord on the right (silk sign). Both testes descended. Left side normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Right inguinal hernia in an infant (reducible)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Right inguinal hernia, reducible, 4-month-old ex-34-week infant. Book prompt elective herniotomy (paediatric surgery); counsel parents on signs of incarceration.

mustExclude.note: Watchful waiting is an adult option; infants have the highest incarceration risk.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Add a paediatric inguinal hernia protocol (herniotomy, prompt repair, no mesh, no truss) selected when age < 16.

mustExclude.note: Paediatric inguinal hernia is treated by herniotomy (high ligation of the sac), not adult mesh repair; adult pre-op items are wrong for an infant.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Age-gate the hernia protocol and prompt (paediatric herniotomy template; suppress adult pre-op items such as PSA/ECG).

guideline.name: EUPSA guideline — surgical management of paediatric inguinal hernia
guideline.section: Timing of repair (infants: early repair; incarceration risk while waiting); open vs laparoscopic herniotomy; management of incarcerated hernia (reduction then repair)
guideline.citation: Morini F, Dreuning KMA, Janssen Lok MJH, et al. Surgical management of pediatric inguinal hernia: a systematic review and guideline from the European Pediatric Surgeons' Association Evidence and Guideline Committee. Eur J Pediatr Surg. 2022;32:219–232.

rationale: Base paediatric case (age 0 years = 4 months). Tests that adult defaults (watchful waiting, mesh, TAPP operative plan, adult pre-operative bloods) are not applied to an infant.
